newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TV TENDER VOTE NOT DECISIVE,ANOTHER NEEDED.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TV TENDER VOTE NOT DECISIVE,ANOTHER NEEDED.

text.p: Hungary's radio and television body ORTT said on Wednesday it could not select the winning bidders for seven-year concession in two national commercial TV channels as none of the bidders received the needed two thirds majority during a voting by board members.
"The second vote will probably be held on Monday," ORTT spokesman Gyorgy Lovas told Reuters.
Three bidders are in the race for ten-year concessions for two national commercial TV channels, on offer for eight billion forints plus 25 per cent VAT each, three years payable in advance.

The Swedish-Hungarian consortium of SBS-MTM submitted a bid for one channel, a consortium of CLT and UFA for the other while U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises (CME) is in the race for both.
Five of the eight-person ORTT board are delegated by opposition parties, two other members are delegated by the ruling parties while the president of the board is neutral.
Under Hungary's media law the president is not entitled to vote in the first round.
The president plus the two delegates of the ruling parties have a combined voting power equal to that of the five opposition delegates but the president has no veto right.
